items.body:
## Summary

LeRobot supports **reading** Lance-backed datasets through `BaseDatasetReader`, `LanceDatasetReader`, and storage-format routing. Dataset creation, recording, resume, publishing, and editing remain available only for the default Parquet/MP4 format.

The write path has already been separated from `LeRobotDataset`: a dedicated `DatasetWriter` owns the current Parquet/MP4 implementation, while `LeRobotDataset.add_frame()`, `save_episode()`, `clear_episode_buffer()`, and `finalize()` delegate to it.

The missing piece is therefore not extracting the write implementation again, but:

1. defining a complete storage-backend-aware writer contract;
2. routing creation and resume by `storage_format`;
3. adding a native Lance writer;
4. defining dataset-level visibility across `frames`, `videos`, and metadata;
5. making reads, resume, and recovery use the same committed version vector.

This proposal introduces:

1. an immediate guard against resuming a non-default dataset with the default writer;
2. a formal writer contract covering all current consumers, including cleanup and interrupt paths;
3. unified storage-backend routing for readers and writers;
4. metadata plumbing that persists non-default `storage_format` values without changing existing default-format `info.json` files;
5. a native local `LanceDatasetWriter`, starting with tabular-only datasets;
6. an explicit dataset-level commit protocol across `frames`, `videos`, and metadata;
7. manifest-aware reads, deterministic crash recovery, and safe resume;
8. a staged path to video recording, publishing, and native editing.

Source baseline: LeRobot `main` at commit [`5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/tree/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed). All line numbers and source links below refer to that commit.

**Scope note:** Phase 0 and Phase 1 are independent of Lance write support. They fix an existing unsafe resume path and formalize the writer boundary for any future backend. They can land before the Lance implementation.

---

## Motivation

The current Lance integration is intentionally read-only. It supports map-style training from Lance tables stored locally, on the Hub, or in compatible object stores while preserving the public `LeRobotDataset` item interface. See #4363.

Today, creating a Lance-backed LeRobot dataset requires:

1. recording or creating a regular Parquet/MP4 dataset;
2. finalizing it;
3. converting it with external `lerobot-lancedb` tooling;
4. uploading or copying the converted dataset separately.

This is also how the current tests create Lance fixtures:

- [`tests/datasets/test_lance_backend.py:27-33`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/tests/datasets/test_lance_backend.py#L27-L33) imports `lerobot_lancedb.convert`;
- [`full_tests.yml:92-93`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/.github/workflows/full_tests.yml#L92-L93) installs the converter for the Lance backend tests.

There is no in-tree way to:

- record directly into Lance;
- append episodes to an existing Lance dataset;
- safely resume interrupted Lance recording;
- publish a locally created Lance dataset through LeRobot;
- perform Lance-native editing through LeRobot APIs.

Lance provides useful table-level primitives such as append, versioned commits, deletion vectors, updates, schema evolution, column addition, time travel, and compaction. These can avoid rewriting unrelated data, but they do **not** by themselves provide a transaction across LeRobot's separate `frames`, `videos`, and metadata tables.

This proposal therefore defines dataset-level visibility explicitly instead of claiming cross-table ACID semantics.

This work supports future dataset editing, reward and quality annotation, additional modalities, and reproducible version pinning. It may improve recording recovery, but it does **not** replace capture-side validation for dropped frames, missing images, encoder failures, or buffer overflows.

---

## Current state

### Reader architecture

```text
LeRobotDataset
  |
  +-- loads meta/info.json["storage_format"]
  |
  +-- make_dataset_reader(storage_format, backend_options)
        |
        +-- DatasetReader            # default Parquet/MP4
        |
        +-- LanceDatasetReader       # frames.lance / videos.lance / meta.lance
```

[`storage.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/storage.py) contains the reader registry and lazily imports optional backends.

[`LanceDatasetReader`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_backend.py) implements the same frame-level item contract as the default reader.

For a non-default storage format, `LeRobotDataset.__init__()` constructs the backend reader, sets `writer = None`, and returns in read-only mode:

- [`lerobot_dataset.py:289-310`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py#L289-L310)

### Writer architecture

The default write path is already encapsulated in [`DatasetWriter`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_writer.py).

It owns:

- the episode buffer;
- asynchronous image writing;
- Parquet writer state;
- streaming, immediate, and batched video encoding;
- per-episode statistics;
- metadata updates;
- finalization and cleanup.

`LeRobotDataset.create()` and `LeRobotDataset.resume()` still construct this concrete writer directly:

- [`lerobot_dataset.py:838-846`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py#L838-L846)
- [`lerobot_dataset.py:956-965`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py#L956-L965)

The missing route is:

```text
storage_format
  |
  +-- storage backend
        |
        +-- DATASET_READER
        +-- optional DATASET_WRITER
        +-- format version
        +-- capabilities
```

### Writer consumers outside the facade

The writer is not consumed only through `LeRobotDataset.add_frame()` and `save_episode()`.

Cleanup, RL, and image-writing paths access it directly:

| Call site | Current access | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| [`video_utils.py:1276-1286`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/video_utils.py#L1276-L1286) | `_streaming_encoder`, `cancel_pending_videos()`, `cleanup_interrupted_episode()` | Runs from `VideoEncodingManager.__exit__()`, including exception paths |
| [`image_writer.py:29-39`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/image_writer.py#L29-L39) | `writer.image_writer.stop()` | Exception cleanup performed by `safe_stop_image_writer` |
| [`lerobot_dataset.py:848-849`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py#L848-L849) | `start_image_writer()` | Create path |
| [`lerobot_dataset.py:967-968`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py#L967-L968) | `start_image_writer()` | Resume path |
| [`rl/buffer.py:562`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/rl/buffer.py#L562) | `start_image_writer()` | RL dataset construction |
| [`rl/buffer.py:605`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/rl/buffer.py#L605) | `stop_image_writer()` | RL cleanup |
| [`rl/gym_manipulator.py:767-769`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/rl/gym_manipulator.py#L767-L769) | `writer.image_writer` and `.stop()` | `finally` cleanup |

An abstraction covering only the facade is incomplete.

A new backend must never trigger a secondary `AttributeError` while another exception is already being handled.

### Metadata plumbing gap

`storage_format` is readable but cannot currently be set through dataset creation:

- [`DatasetInfo.storage_format`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/utils.py#L184-L187) exists and defaults to `None`;
- [`DatasetInfo.to_dict()`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/utils.py#L212-L227) omits the key when unset;
- [`LeRobotDatasetMetadata.storage_format`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_metadata.py#L361-L364) falls back to the default format;
- [`LeRobotDatasetMetadata.create()`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_metadata.py#L787-L862) has no `storage_format` parameter;
- [`create_empty_dataset_info()`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/feature_utils.py#L83-L118) cannot set the field either.

For compatibility, the public creation parameter should default to `None`, not the literal string `"lerobot"`.

`None` means the effective default backend while preserving the existing serialized `info.json`. Only non-default formats should write the field.

### `resume()` can select the wrong writer

`LeRobotDataset.resume()` loads metadata and then unconditionally constructs the default `DatasetWriter`; it never checks `meta.storage_format`:

- [`lerobot_dataset.py:935-965`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py#L935-L965)

Calling `resume()` on a Lance dataset does not fail immediately. It returns an object configured with the Parquet/MP4 writer. A subsequent frame or episode write can therefore create default-layout artifacts inside a Lance root.

This differs from `push_to_hub()`, which fails loudly for non-default formats:

- [`lerobot_dataset.py:653-657`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lerobot_dataset.py#L653-L657)

This is an existing correctness defect independent of Lance writer support.

### Metadata persistence is not episode-atomic

The current metadata implementation intentionally buffers episode rows:

- `_save_episode_metadata()` appends episode metadata to an in-memory buffer;
- the buffer is flushed only when `metadata_buffer_size` is reached or metadata is finalized;
- the episode Parquet writer remains open until finalization;
- `info.json` and `stats.json`, however, are updated on every `save_episode()`.

See:

- [`dataset_metadata.py:151-207`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_metadata.py#L151-L207)
- [`dataset_metadata.py:567-636`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_metadata.py#L567-L636)
- [`dataset_metadata.py:638-678`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_metadata.py#L638-L678)

Therefore a Lance writer cannot safely call the current metadata mutators and then publish `meta.lance`.

`info.json` may already declare episode N while the corresponding episode metadata row is still buffered or the Parquet footer is not yet closed.

A Lance commit needs a complete metadata snapshot per published dataset commit.

### The current Lance reader always opens latest table versions

`LanceDatasetReader._ensure_open()` directly opens `frames` and `videos`, validates them against the already-loaded metadata, and addresses frame rows by physical position:

- [`lance_backend.py:231-271`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_backend.py#L231-L271)

It does not resolve a dataset-level commit or pin each table to a referenced version.

Remote metadata materialization also opens the latest `meta` table and returns early if a local `meta/` directory already exists:

- [`lance_utils.py:270-301`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_utils.py#L270-L301)

A writer-side manifest alone is therefore insufficient. The reader and metadata-loading path must become manifest-aware before crash-safe writes can be claimed.

### Lance schema assumptions

The native reader currently:

- rejects image-backed features:
  [`lance_backend.py:127-131`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_backend.py#L127-L131);
- requires episode ranges to tile `[0, total_frames)` contiguously:
  [`lance_backend.py:159-169`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_backend.py#L159-L169);
- requires `frames.count_rows() == meta.total_frames`:
  [`lance_backend.py:238-243`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_backend.py#L238-L243);
- uses `Permutation.identity(table)` and therefore physical row order:
  [`lance_backend.py:245-247`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_backend.py#L245-L247);
- maps feature names with `key.replace(".", "_")`:
  [`lance_utils.py:236-237`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/lance_utils.py#L236-L237).

The column-name mapping is not injective. For example, `a.b` and `a_b` map to the same Lance column.

Current generic feature-name validation only rejects `/`, so the Lance backend must perform its own collision and reserved-column checks before creating a dataset.

### Editing tools remain default-layout-specific

The current editing utilities are coupled to the default layout:

- [`delete_episodes()`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_tools.py#L107) creates a new dataset, rewrites and reindexes tabular data, remaps episode indices, and may re-encode video;
- [`modify_tasks()`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_tools.py#L1459) updates task metadata and Parquet columns in place;
- [`add_features()`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/5aa74557f84c54d4b458f8b9643c5aa2982acfed/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_tools.py#L421) delegates to `modify_features()`, which creates a new dataset and copies data.

These operations cannot be replaced by one raw Lance `delete()`, `update()`, or `add_columns()` call because LeRobot also maintains indices, contiguous episode boundaries, task mappings, statistics, video references, and metadata invariants.

---

## Goals

### Primary

- Route dataset creation and resume to a writer selected by storage format.
- Preserve existing Parquet/MP4 behavior and serialized metadata.
- Support native local creation and append for tabular Lance datasets.
- Preserve item-level, metadata-level, and statistics compatibility across formats.
- Define explicit dataset-level visibility semantics across all Lance tables.
- Make readers, writers, and resume resolve the same committed version vector.
- Support deterministic crash recovery and safe resume.
- Keep Lance dependencies optional and lazily imported.
- Reject unsupported backend capabilities before creating or mutating the target root.

### Secondary

- Native video-backed Lance recording.
- Native publishing of locally created Lance datasets.
- Dataset-level version pinning and tags.
- Fragment compaction and old-version retention policies.
- A safe foundation for Lance-native editing.

---

## Non-goals for the initial implementation

The first implementation does not include:

- Lance-native `delete_episodes`, `modify_tasks`, or feature addition;
- image-backed Lance datasets;
- concurrent multi-writer recording;
- direct recording into remote object-store URIs;
- automatic remote publishing;
- shared MP4 chunks across episodes;
- unconditional compaction or old-version deletion;
- replacing LeRobot statistics with SQL;
- claiming cross-table ACID transactions.

Although concurrent writers are a non-goal, the local writer must still acquire an exclusive dataset lock so two processes cannot accidentally write the same root.

---

## Proposed design

### 1. Formalize the writer contract

The contract must cover the facade and all live cleanup paths.

It should expose behavior rather than concrete resources such as `_streaming_encoder` or `image_writer`.

```python
class BaseDatasetWriter(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def add_frame(self, frame: dict) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def save_episode(
        self,
        episode_data: dict | None = None,
        parallel_encoding: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def clear_episode_buffer(self, delete_images: bool = True) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def has_pending_frames(self) -> bool:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def abort_episode(self, episode_index: int) -> None:
        """Cancel backend work and remove uncommitted episode artifacts."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def start_image_writer(
        self,
        num_processes: int = 0,
        num_threads: int = 4,
    ) -> None:
        raise UnsupportedWriterCapability("async_image_writing")

    def stop_image_writer(self) -> None:
        """Idempotent cleanup; a backend without this resource is a no-op."""

    @abstractmethod
    def finalize(self) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError
```

`LeRobotDataset.has_pending_frames()` becomes a delegation.

`episode_buffer` may remain an implementation detail on the default writer during migration, but it should not be required by the backend contract.

`VideoEncodingManager.__exit__()` should call:

```python
writer.abort_episode(self.dataset.num_episodes)
```

on failure instead of reading `_streaming_encoder`.

`safe_stop_image_writer`, `rl/buffer.py`, and `rl/gym_manipulator.py` should call the public, idempotent `stop_image_writer()` method instead of inspecting `writer.image_writer`.

The existing class becomes:

```python
class ParquetDatasetWriter(BaseDatasetWriter):
    ...
```

Keep the following temporary compatibility alias:

```python
DatasetWriter = ParquetDatasetWriter
```

A backend declining a capability must fail during preflight or raise a clear `UnsupportedWriterCapability`. It must never fail with `AttributeError` during exception handling.

### 2. Use one storage-backend registration source

Avoid separate reader and writer registries that can drift.

Reuse the existing backend module registry as the source of truth and allow every backend module to expose an optional writer:

```python
# lance_backend.py

DATASET_READER = LanceDatasetReader
DATASET_WRITER = LanceDatasetWriter

STORAGE_FORMAT_VERSION = 1

WRITER_CAPABILITIES = frozenset(
    {
        "tabular",
        "resume",
        "dataset_commits",
    }
)
```

The default format remains built in and must not import optional dependencies.

```python
def make_dataset_reader(
    storage_format: str,
    **kwargs,
) -> BaseDatasetReader:
    return resolve_storage_backend(storage_format).reader(**kwargs)

def make_dataset_writer(
    storage_format: str,
    **kwargs,
) -> BaseDatasetWriter:
    backend = resolve_storage_backend(storage_format)

    if backend.writer is None:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"No writer is registered for storage_format={storage_format!r}"
        )

    return backend.writer(**kwargs)
```

If entry-point discovery from #4576 lands, reader and writer discovery should use the same backend entry point rather than independent reader and writer groups.

### 3. Validate before creating the dataset root

`LeRobotDataset.create()` gains:

```python
storage_format: str | None = None
```

`None` means the effective default format.

The value stored in `DatasetInfo` must remain `None` for the default backend so existing default-format `info.json` files do not gain a new field.

Before calling `LeRobotDatasetMetadata.create()` or creating files, `create()` must:

1. resolve the backend;
2. verify that a writer exists;
3. import and validate optional dependencies;
4. validate feature and modality support;
5. validate backend-specific schema rules;
6. reject column-name collisions and reserved names;
7. reject unsupported options such as image-backed Lance or async image-writing for the tabular MVP.

For Lance, the column mapping must be injective.

If `to_lance_column()` remains:

```python
key.replace(".", "_")
```

creation must reject any feature set for which two logical names map to the same physical column.

It must also reject collisions with backend-reserved columns.

Only non-default formats are persisted:

```python
effective_format = storage_format or DEFAULT_STORAGE_FORMAT

metadata_storage_format = (
    None
    if effective_format == DEFAULT_STORAGE_FORMAT
    else effective_format
)
```

`LeRobotDatasetMetadata.create()` and `create_empty_dataset_info()` must accept and propagate `metadata_storage_format`.

### 4. Keep orchestration in `LeRobotDataset`

The backend writer must not duplicate public constructors.

```python
dataset = LeRobotDataset.create(
    repo_id="user/dataset",
    fps=30,
    features=features,
    storage_format="lance",
)
```

Creation should:

1. preflight the selected backend;
2. create metadata with `storage_format="lance"`;
3. create the empty backend tables and genesis commit;
4. construct the writer through `make_dataset_writer()`;
5. return the normal write-mode facade.

```python
dataset = LeRobotDataset.resume(
    repo_id="user/dataset",
    root="./dataset",
)
```

Resume should:

1. determine the storage format;
2. resolve the latest complete dataset commit;
3. materialize the committed metadata snapshot;
4. validate frame, episode, task, video, schema, and version invariants;
5. acquire the local writer lock;
6. construct the matching writer;
7. continue from the committed frame and episode totals.

### 5. Separate metadata calculation from persistence

The current metadata object mixes state calculation with immediate file writes and buffered Parquet writers.

A Lance commit needs an immutable, complete metadata snapshot before publication.

Introduce a prepare/install boundary conceptually equivalent to:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PreparedEpisodeCommit:
    episode_index: int
    episode_length: int
    episode_row: dict
    tasks: Any
    info: DatasetInfo
    stats: dict

prepared = meta.prepare_episode_commit(
    episode_index=episode_index,
    episode_length=episode_length,
    episode_tasks=episode_tasks,
    episode_stats=episode_stats,
    episode_metadata=episode_metadata,
)
```

`prepare_episode_commit()` calculates the next metadata state without:

- writing durable metadata files;
- advancing committed in-memory totals;
- replacing the currently visible dataset state.

The writer then stages data and metadata, publishes the dataset commit, and only afterwards installs the new committed state:

```python
frames_version = writer.stage_frames(prepared)

videos_version = writer.stage_videos(prepared)  # video phase only

meta_version = writer.stage_metadata_snapshot(prepared)

commit_id = writer.publish_commit(
    parent_commit_id=current_commit_id,
    frames_version=frames_version,
    videos_version=videos_version,
    meta_version=meta_version,
)

meta.install_committed_state(prepared)
```

The default writer may continue using the existing buffered implementation initially.

The prepare/install API is required for Lance, where each published commit must reference a fully readable metadata snapshot.

For Lance, `metadata_buffer_size` must not delay committed episode metadata. It should either be rejected for Lance or documented as unused by the Lance metadata snapshot path.

### 6. Lance storage layout

The writer produces the layout expected by the native reader plus a dataset commit table:

```text
<root>/
├── frames.lance
├── videos.lance          # introduced in the video phase
├── meta.lance
├── commits.lance
└── meta/                 # working/cache materialization, not commit authority
    ├── info.json
    ├── stats.json
    ├── tasks.parquet
    └── episodes/
        └── chunk-000/
            └── file-000.parquet
```

#### `frames.lance`

One row per frame containing the non-video features required by the reader:

- `index`;
- `episode_index`;
- `frame_index`;
- `timestamp`;
- `task_index`;
- actions;
- states;
- strings;
- language columns;
- other tabular features.

Column names use the existing reader mapping, subject to collision and reserved-name validation.

#### `videos.lance`

For the initial video writer, one row represents one immutable MP4 blob for one `(episode, camera)` pair:

- `video_key`;
- `chunk_index`;
- `file_index`;
- the blob-v2 video column;
- `file_size`;
- `moov_offset`;
- `moov_size`;
- `kf_indices`;
- `kf_positions`.

Each episode receives a unique logical `(video_key, chunk_index, file_index)` locator and starts at:

```text
from_timestamp = 0
```

This remains compatible with the current reader schema while avoiding replacement of an existing shared MP4 blob during recording.

Shared multi-episode MP4 chunks can be introduced later as an explicit compaction optimization. They must not be part of the initial crash-consistent writer.

#### `meta.lance`

Each `meta.lance` version represents a complete metadata snapshot as `(path, data)` rows.

The snapshot includes every file under `meta/` required to load that commit.

Paths must be normalized relative POSIX paths.

The writer must reject:

- absolute paths;
- `..` traversal;
- duplicate paths;
- paths escaping the metadata root.

For manifest-backed Lance datasets, the `meta.lance` version referenced by the dataset commit is authoritative.

The local `meta/` directory is a working or cached materialization and may be rebuilt from the committed snapshot after a crash.

#### `commits.lance`

One row represents one complete dataset commit.

This is the dataset-level visibility point.

```json
{
  "format_version": 1,
  "commit_id": 42,
  "parent_commit_id": 41,
  "total_episodes": 42,
  "total_frames": 125430,
  "frames_version": 43,
  "videos_version": 18,
  "meta_version": 43,
  "schema_hash": "sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

For a tabular-only dataset, `videos_version` is null.

The initial empty dataset has a genesis commit.

Writers append one commit row only after every referenced table version has been created and validated.

### 7. Manifest-aware reader bootstrap

Dataset-level commits are useful only if every read opens the referenced table versions.

For a manifest-backed Lance dataset, loading must follow this order:

```text
recognize Lance root
  -> read latest valid row from commits.lance
  -> open meta.lance at commit.meta_version
  -> materialize that metadata snapshot
  -> load LeRobotDatasetMetadata
  -> open frames.lance at commit.frames_version
  -> open videos.lance at commit.videos_version, if present
  -> validate totals, schema, episodes, tasks, and video references
```

The implementation must pin each table handle to the recorded version using the version-aware API supported by the pinned `lancedb` dependency.

Opening the latest table version is not sufficient.

This requires changing both:

- `LanceDatasetReader._ensure_open()`, which currently opens the latest `frames` and `videos` versions;
- metadata loading/materialization, which currently loads `meta/` before the reader is constructed and reuses an existing local directory without checking a dataset commit.

Remote metadata caches should be keyed by at least:

```text
root + Hub revision + dataset commit_id
```

or:

```text
root + Hub revision + meta_version
```

This prevents two committed dataset snapshots from reusing incompatible metadata.

### 8. Legacy Lance datasets without `commits.lance`

Existing converted Lance datasets must remain readable.

#### Read

If no commit table exists, preserve the current read-only behavior:

- open the latest tables;
- run the current consistency checks;
- do not require a dataset commit.

#### Resume/write

Before the first native append:

1. validate the latest `frames`, optional `videos`, and metadata as one consistent state;
2. capture their current table versions;
3. create a genesis dataset commit referencing those versions;
4. only then construct a native writer.

If validation fails, abort without modifying the dataset.

No writer may append to a manifest-less dataset before a validated genesis commit exists.

### 9. Episode write flow

#### Tabular MVP

`save_episode()` should:

1. validate the episode buffer with the existing rules;
2. assign `index`, `episode_index`, `frame_index`, `timestamp`, and `task_index`;
3. compute statistics with the existing `compute_episode_stats()` implementation;
4. prepare the next complete metadata state without publishing it;
5. append frame rows to `frames.lance`;
6. capture the resulting frame-table version;
7. write a complete `meta.lance` snapshot;
8. capture the resulting metadata-table version;
9. reopen the exact staged versions and validate:
   - frame count;
   - episode boundaries;
   - task mappings;
   - metadata totals;
   - schema hash;
10. append the dataset commit row to `commits.lance`;
11. install or materialize the committed metadata state;
12. clear the episode buffer.

Statistics must reuse the current implementation to preserve:

- shape handling;
- min, max, mean, std, and count;
- histogram-based quantiles;
- image sampling semantics;
- RGB normalization;
- depth behavior.

If an operation before commit publication fails, the previous dataset commit remains visible.

The writer must either:

- retain a valid retryable episode buffer; or
- mark the current episode aborted and require `clear_episode_buffer()`.

It must not leave a partially mutated buffer after removing `size` or `task`.

#### Video phase

The initial video implementation should:

1. finish staged camera frames or streaming encoders;
2. encode each camera to a temporary MP4;
3. validate frame count, duration, codec metadata, and byte-index data;
4. append one immutable MP4 blob row per `(episode, camera)`;
5. append frame rows;
6. prepare and write the complete metadata snapshot;
7. validate all referenced video rows and exact table versions;
8. publish the dataset commit;
9. delete temporary media only after publication succeeds.

No episode becomes visible before all required video assets, frame rows, and metadata are referenced by one published commit.

### 10. Dataset-level commit semantics

Lance commits each table independently.

A successful append to one table is not a transaction across all LeRobot tables.

```text
prepare and validate episode
  -> write videos table version      # video phase only
  -> write frames table version
  -> write complete meta table version
  -> validate exact version vector
  -> append commits.lance row
  -> episode becomes visible
```

On a crash before the final commit-row append:

- the previous dataset commit remains visible;
- new table versions are unreachable from the dataset manifest;
- local metadata is restored from the previous committed `meta_version` on reopen;
- orphaned versions may be cleaned later under an explicit retention policy.

On a crash after commit publication, reopening must expose the new complete version vector.

Recovery must not be described as deleting a failed version.

The supported behavior is:

- ignore table versions not referenced by a dataset commit;
- continue from the latest complete dataset commit;
- clean unreachable versions only through explicit maintenance.

### 11. Local writer locking

The local Lance writer must acquire an exclusive lock for the dataset root before initialization or resume.

It must hold the lock until `finalize()` or abort.

This does not provide multi-writer support. It prevents accidental concurrent writers from publishing conflicting parent commits.

Every dataset commit records `parent_commit_id`.

Publication must verify that the parent still matches the latest committed parent.

Remote distributed locking or conditional commit semantics remain a later feature.

### 12. Resume and recovery

`resume()` should:

1. acquire the writer lock;
2. read the latest valid dataset commit;
3. open every table at the referenced version;
4. materialize committed metadata, ignoring an untrusted newer local working copy;
5. validate:
   - frame count;
   - episode count;
   - contiguous episode boundaries;
   - logical and physical frame order required by the current reader;
   - task indices and task table;
   - referenced videos and byte-index columns;
   - metadata totals;
   - schema and column mapping;
6. identify unreferenced newer versions and temporary artifacts;
7. continue from the committed next episode and frame index.

Old-version cleanup is not part of ordinary resume.

It must be explicit because removing versions destroys time-travel capability and may invalidate dataset tags.

### 13. Version pinning and tags

Lance versions are table-local, so a reproducible dataset version must identify the complete version vector:

```text
dataset tag
  -> dataset commit_id
  -> frames version
  -> videos version
  -> meta version
  -> storage-format version
  -> schema version
```

A future API may expose:

```python
dataset.create_tag("quality-v1")

dataset = LeRobotDataset(
    repo_id="user/dataset",
    dataset_version="quality-v1",
)
```

The reader resolves the tag to a dataset commit and opens all tables at the recorded versions.

The relationship between Hub revisions, dataset commits, and Lance table versions must be documented explicitly.

### 14. Fragment and version maintenance

Per-episode append is the simplest correctness model but may create many fragments for datasets containing short episodes.

The initial implementation should favor correctness and collect:

- fragments per episode;
- append latency;
- `save_episode()` P50/P95;
- reader startup latency;
- metadata growth;
- compaction cost;
- version count;
- object-store request count where applicable.

A later optimization may batch already-completed episodes into one append while preserving the same dataset-level commit semantics.

`finalize()` may expose configurable compaction, but it must not:

- compact unconditionally;
- make recording shutdown unexpectedly expensive;
- remove old versions by default.

### 15. Native publishing

`push_to_hub()` currently rejects non-default formats, so Lance publishing is a missing implementation.

A Lance-aware publisher must define:

- which `.lance` directories and metadata files are uploaded;
- whether publication includes complete history or only a retained snapshot;
- how `commits.lance` and referenced versions are preserved;
- how dataset tags map to Hub revisions;
- whether publication is a full snapshot or incremental sync;
- how interrupted upload is detected;
- how a clean client verifies and opens the published commit.

Direct recording into an object-store URI is separate from publishing a local Lance dataset and should not be bundled into the first publishing PR.

### 16. Future native editing

Native editing should follow only after the writer and dataset commit model are stable.

#### `delete_episodes`

A delete must update:

- visible frame rows;
- episode and global indices;
- episode metadata;
- tasks;
- splits;
- statistics;
- video references;
- the dataset commit.

A raw Lance deletion tombstone is not currently sufficient because the reader:

- requires physical row count to equal `total_frames`;
- requires episode ranges to tile `[0, total_frames)`;
- reads rows by physical position.

Before enabling native delete, choose one of:

- reindex and rewrite retained logical rows;
- make the reader resolve the explicit `index` column;
- use stable row IDs plus a logical-order mapping;
- represent edits as immutable dataset views.

#### `modify_tasks`

Task edits affect:

- frame-level `task_index`;
- episode task metadata;
- `tasks.parquet`;
- `total_tasks`;
- the dataset commit.

In-place updates must not be enabled while frame lookup assumes stable physical position.

A separate task-mapping table may be preferable.

#### `add_features`

Column-local feature addition is a strong Lance use case for:

- rewards;
- embeddings;
- annotations;
- predictions;
- filtering and quality flags.

It must still:

- update `info.json["features"]`;
- compute statistics for the new feature;
- verify alignment with logical frame indices;
- publish a new dataset commit.

---

## Implementation plan

### Phase 0 — storage-format guard for `resume()`

Independent; no Lance dependency.

- Read `meta.storage_format` before constructing the writer.
- Raise `NotImplementedError` for non-default formats until a writer is registered.
- Add a regression test proving that `resume()` on a Lance dataset fails before creating:
  - `data/**/*.parquet`;
  - `videos/`;
  - image staging files.

This closes the current wrong-writer path immediately.

### Phase 1 — writer contract and backend routing

Pure refactoring; no Lance dependency required for default-format tests.

- Add `BaseDatasetWriter`.
- Rename the current writer to `ParquetDatasetWriter`.
- Retain `DatasetWriter` as a compatibility alias.
- Delegate `LeRobotDataset.has_pending_frames()` to the writer.
- Add `abort_episode()`.
- Add idempotent image-writer lifecycle methods.
- Remove production reads of `_streaming_encoder`.
- Remove production reads of `image_writer`.
- Update:
  - `VideoEncodingManager`;
  - `safe_stop_image_writer`;
  - `rl/buffer.py`;
  - `rl/gym_manipulator.py`.
- Reuse one storage-backend registry for reader and optional writer discovery.
- Add `storage_format: str | None = None` to creation and metadata plumbing.
- Validate the selected backend before creating or mutating the root.
- Add a stub non-default writer proving routing works without Lance.

### Phase 2 — dataset snapshot protocol and manifest-aware reads

- Introduce `commits.lance`.
- Introduce the genesis commit.
- Add version-vector resolution.
- Pin `meta`, `frames`, and optional `videos` to committed versions.
- Make metadata materialization commit-aware.
- Introduce prepared metadata snapshots.
- Add local writer locking.
- Add parent-commit validation.
- Preserve read-only compatibility for legacy manifest-less Lance datasets.
- Add validated genesis migration before native resume of a legacy dataset.

This phase must land before claiming crash-safe native writes.

### Phase 3 — local tabular Lance writer

- Create an empty `frames.lance` schema.
- Validate logical-to-physical column mappings.
- Validate reserved columns.
- Append tabular episodes.
- Reuse current frame validation.
- Reuse current statistics.
- Write complete metadata snapshots.
- Publish one dataset commit per completed episode.
- Implement resume from the committed version vector.
- Add:
  - round-trip parity tests;
  - lock tests;
  - legacy migration tests;
  - failure-injection tests.

### Phase 4 — video-backed Lance writer

- Use one immutable MP4 blob per `(episode, camera)` initially.
- Reuse existing encoders.
- Validate media before publication.
- Build the reader's required byte-index columns.
- Integrate video, frame, metadata, and dataset commit versions.
- Test:
  - RGB;
  - multiple cameras;
  - depth video;
  - interrupted encoding;
  - temporary-file cleanup.

Shared multi-episode video chunks remain a later compaction feature.

### Phase 5 — recording CLI integration

```text
lerobot-record --dataset.storage_format=lance
```

- Add `storage_format` to `DatasetRecordConfig`.
- Route it through all recording and rollout creation paths.
- Add configuration validation.
- Reject image-backed Lance mode clearly.
- Add resume and kill/restart integration tests.
- Add local recording benchmarks.

### Phase 6 — Lance-aware publishing and remote writing

- Publish a local manifest-backed Lance dataset.
- Reload from a clean cache.
- Preserve the committed version vector.
- Preserve dataset tags.
- Define retained-history policy.
- Add:
  - authentication tests;
  - interruption tests;
  - conflict tests;
  - clean-client verification tests.
- Design remote commit locking separately from local recording.

### Follow-up RFCs

- shared-video compaction;
- feature addition;
- task modification;
- episode deletion;
- immutable dataset views;
- fragment cleanup;
- version cleanup.

---

## Compatibility

- Existing callers continue to use the effective `"lerobot"` backend.
- The public default is `storage_format=None`, preserving existing `info.json`.
- Datasets without a `storage_format` field remain default Parquet/MP4 datasets.
- `ParquetDatasetWriter` behavior and file layout remain unchanged.
- `DatasetWriter` remains a temporary alias.
- Importing LeRobot or using the default format must not import LanceDB.
- Lance dependencies load only when Lance reading, writing, migration, or maintenance is selected.
- Existing converted Lance datasets remain readable without a commit table.
- Native append requires a validated genesis dataset commit.

---

## Testing and acceptance criteria

### Writer abstraction

- The complete default-format test suite passes unchanged except for intentional private-attribute test updates.
- No default public API or file-layout change.
- Default `info.json` still omits `storage_format`.
- `LeRobotDataset.has_pending_frames()` behavior remains unchanged.
- No production caller reads `_streaming_encoder`.
- No production caller reads `image_writer`.
- `VideoEncodingManager`, `safe_stop_image_writer`, `rl/buffer.py`, and `rl/gym_manipulator.py` have explicit coverage.
- Cleanup methods are idempotent.
- A declined capability produces a clear backend error, never an `AttributeError` during exception handling.

### Backend routing and validation

- A registered read-only backend fails clearly when selected for creation or resume.
- Missing optional dependencies fail before the target root is created or modified.
- Unsupported image-backed Lance creation fails before any table or metadata is written.
- Feature-name mapping collisions such as `a.b` versus `a_b` fail before creation.
- Reserved-column collisions fail before creation.
- Existing default callers require no new arguments.

### Dataset commit protocol

- Every manifest-backed read resolves a dataset commit before loading metadata.
- The reader opens the exact `frames`, `videos`, and `meta` versions referenced by that commit.
- The reader does not silently open the latest versions.
- Every published commit references a complete metadata snapshot.
- A local `meta/` directory newer than the latest commit is ignored or replaced on reopen.
- A missing referenced table version fails loudly.
- An invalid referenced table version fails loudly.
- A second local writer cannot acquire the dataset lock.
- Parent-commit mismatch prevents publication.

### Legacy Lance compatibility

- Manifest-less converted datasets remain readable.
- Native resume validates current latest tables and metadata before creating a genesis commit.
- Failed validation leaves the legacy dataset unchanged.
- After genesis creation, repeated resume/finalize cycles use the dataset commit protocol.

### Tabular round trip

For the same frames, Parquet and Lance produce equivalent:

- item keys and values;
- dtypes and shapes;
- timestamps;
- global indices;
- episode indices;
- frame indices;
- task indices;
- task strings;
- delta-timestamp windows;
- padding masks;
- episode metadata;
- dataset statistics.

Run parity tests with `metadata_buffer_size > 1` to prove that a Lance commit never exposes buffered or incomplete episode metadata.

### Video round trip

- single camera;
- multiple cameras;
- one immutable blob per episode and camera;
- RGB video;
- depth video;
- frame count validation;
- duration validation;
- timestamp tolerance;
- byte-index correctness;
- random reads;
- batched reads;
- DataLoader worker compatibility;
- interruption before, during, and after encoding.

### Failure injection

Terminate or raise:

1. before media encoding;
2. during media encoding;
3. after video-table append;
4. after frame-table append;
5. while building the metadata snapshot;
6. after metadata-table write;
7. before commit publication;
8. during commit publication;
9. immediately after commit publication;
10. before local metadata materialization completes.

After restart, the dataset must expose exactly:

- the previous committed episode count; or
- the new committed episode count.

It must never expose frame, video, and metadata states from different dataset commits.

### Resume

- append after normal shutdown;
- append after process termination;
- append with unreferenced newer table versions present;
- append when local metadata is ahead of the committed snapshot;
- append after compaction;
- append after validated legacy genesis migration;
- repeated finalize/resume cycles;
- clear failure when the writer lock is held;
- clear failure when a referenced committed version is missing.

### Benchmarks

Measure:

- frames per second;
- `save_episode()` P50/P95;
- peak memory;
- disk size;
- fragment count;
- version count;
- reader startup latency;
- resume latency;
- metadata snapshot cost;
- compaction cost;
- object-store request count where applicable.

Cover:

- long episodes;
- many short episodes;
- tabular-only datasets;
- one camera;
- multiple cameras.

### Publishing

After upload:

- load from a clean cache;
- resolve the expected dataset commit;
- open the exact referenced table versions;
- iterate all frames;
- decode all video variants;
- verify dataset tag resolution;
- compare metadata with the local source;
- compare statistics with the local source;
- detect interrupted or incomplete publication.

---

## Open questions

1. **Writer interface type:** ABC or `Protocol`? The required behavior should remain the same either way.
2. **Backend registration compatibility:** rename the current reader-module registry to a general backend registry, or retain its name temporarily while allowing modules to expose `DATASET_WRITER`?
3. **Reader row addressing for future editing:** explicit `index` lookup, stable row IDs plus a logical-order map, reindex-on-edit, or immutable views?
4. **Remote writing target:** HF Storage Buckets, `hf://datasets/<namespace>/<repo>`, generic S3/GCS, or a smaller first target?
5. **Retention:** how many committed, tagged, and unreferenced versions should be retained by default?
6. **Publishing history:** publish full Lance version history or a compacted snapshot containing only versions reachable from selected dataset commits?
7. **Shared video compaction:** when should per-episode blobs be compacted into shared files, and how are tags and old commits protected during replacement?

**Title:** Performance regression in _query_hf_dataset when using delta_timestamps (~40x slower)

---

## Summary

LeRobot v3.0's `_query_hf_dataset` implementation has a severe performance regression when querying multiple indices (e.g., for action horizons with `delta_timestamps`). The current implementation is **~40x slower** than using `select()`.

## Root Cause

In commit `a4aa3164` ("fix data access bottleneck"), the implementation changed from using `select()` to direct indexing:

```python
# Old approach (fast) - used select()
torch.stack(self.hf_dataset.select(q_idx)[key])

# New approach (slow) - direct indexing
# In _query_hf_dataset, it tries column-first access which loads ENTIRE column
torch.stack(self.hf_dataset[key][indices])  # This loads entire column first (~3s)
# Then falls back to row-first
torch.stack(self.hf_dataset[indices][key])  # Still slow compared to select()
```

The column-first approach `hf_dataset[key][indices]` loads the entire column into memory before indexing, which is extremely slow. Even after falling back to row-first access, direct indexing `hf_dataset[indices][key]` is still ~40x slower than using `select()`.

## Benchmark Results

Running on a parquet-based dataset with `delta_timestamps` for 50-frame action horizon:

```
Benchmarking dataset: JianZhou0420/libero_openvla_LeRobotv3_0
  Num samples: 20
  Action horizon: 50

  FPS: 10
  Total frames: 273465

============================================================
BENCHMARK RESULTS
============================================================
1. hf_dataset[i] (single frame):
   0.152s total, 7.6ms per sample

2. hf_dataset.select(indices)[key] (OpenPi's fast approach):
   0.128s total, 6.4ms per sample

3. hf_dataset[indices][key] (LeRobot v3.0's slow approach):
   5.253s total, 262.6ms per sample

4. LeRobotDataset[i] with delta_timestamps (what training uses):
   6.980s total, 349.0ms per sample

============================================================
ANALYSIS
============================================================
select() is 40.6x faster than direct indexing

Estimated time per epoch with current LeRobotDataset:
  26.5 hours (1591 minutes)

Estimated time per epoch with select() fix:
  0.56 hours (34 minutes)
```

| Method | Time per sample | Relative |
|--------|----------------|----------|
| `hf_dataset.select(indices)[key]` | 6.4ms | 1x (baseline) |
| `hf_dataset[indices][key]` | 262.6ms | 41x slower |
| `LeRobotDataset[i]` with delta_timestamps | 349.0ms | 55x slower |

**Impact:** Training time increases from ~34 minutes to ~26.5 hours per epoch.

## Use Case

This affects Pi0/OpenPi style action chunking where we need to query 50-frame action horizons using `delta_timestamps`. This is a common pattern for diffusion-based action prediction models.

```python
# Pi0/OpenPi action chunking pattern
delta_timestamps = {"actions": [t / fps for t in range(50)]}  # 50-frame horizon
dataset = LeRobotDataset(repo_id, delta_timestamps=delta_timestamps)

# Each __getitem__ call queries 50 indices - very slow with current implementation
sample = dataset[i]
```

## Suggested Fix

Use `select()` for multi-index queries in `_query_hf_dataset`:

```python
# Fast approach
torch.stack(self.hf_dataset.select(indices)[key])
```

## Benchmark Script

<details>
<summary>Click to expand benchmark_dataset_loading.py</summary>

```python
"""Benchmark LeRobotDataset loading speed.

Compares different data access methods to measure performance impact
of LeRobot v3.0's slow _query_hf_dataset implementation.

Usage:
    python scripts/benchmark_dataset_loading.py
    python scripts/benchmark_dataset_loading.py --num-samples 100
    python scripts/benchmark_dataset_loading.py --repo-id your/dataset
"""

import argparse
import time

import torch


def benchmark_hf_dataset_direct(dataset, num_samples: int) -> float:
    """Benchmark direct hf_dataset access (no delta_timestamps processing)."""
    start = time.time()
    for i in range(num_samples):
        _ = dataset.hf_dataset[i]
    return time.time() - start


def benchmark_hf_dataset_select(dataset, num_samples: int, horizon: int = 50) -> float:
    """Benchmark hf_dataset.select() for action horizon queries."""
    start = time.time()
    for i in range(num_samples):
        indices = list(range(i, min(i + horizon, len(dataset))))
        _ = torch.stack(dataset.hf_dataset.select(indices)['actions'])
    return time.time() - start


def benchmark_hf_dataset_direct_indexing(dataset, num_samples: int, horizon: int = 50) -> float:
    """Benchmark hf_dataset[indices][key] (LeRobot v3.0's slow approach)."""
    start = time.time()
    for i in range(num_samples):
        indices = list(range(i, min(i + horizon, len(dataset))))
        _ = torch.stack(dataset.hf_dataset[indices]['actions'])
    return time.time() - start


def benchmark_lerobot_dataset(dataset_with_delta, num_samples: int) -> float:
    """Benchmark LeRobotDataset with delta_timestamps (full __getitem__)."""
    start = time.time()
    for i in range(num_samples):
        _ = dataset_with_delta[i]
    return time.time() - start


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Benchmark LeRobotDataset loading speed")
    parser.add_argument("--repo-id", default="JianZhou0420/libero_openvla_LeRobotv3_0",
                        help="HuggingFace dataset repo ID")
    parser.add_argument("--num-samples", type=int, default=50,
                        help="Number of samples to benchmark")
    parser.add_argument("--horizon", type=int, default=50,
                        help="Action horizon for delta_timestamps")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    print(f"Benchmarking dataset: {args.repo_id}")
    print(f"  Num samples: {args.num_samples}")
    print(f"  Action horizon: {args.horizon}")
    print()

    # Import here to see any warnings
    from lerobot.datasets.lerobot_dataset import LeRobotDataset, LeRobotDatasetMetadata

    # Load metadata
    meta = LeRobotDatasetMetadata(args.repo_id)
    fps = meta.fps
    print(f"  FPS: {fps}")
    print(f"  Total frames: {meta.total_frames}")
    print()

    # Load dataset WITHOUT delta_timestamps
    print("Loading dataset without delta_timestamps...")
    dataset_simple = LeRobotDataset(args.repo_id)

    # Load dataset WITH delta_timestamps
    print("Loading dataset with delta_timestamps...")
    delta_timestamps = {"actions": [t / fps for t in range(args.horizon)]}
    dataset_with_delta = LeRobotDataset(args.repo_id, delta_timestamps=delta_timestamps)

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Benchmark 1: Direct hf_dataset access
    elapsed = benchmark_hf_dataset_direct(dataset_simple, args.num_samples)
    print(f"1. hf_dataset[i] (single frame):")
    print(f"   {elapsed:.3f}s total, {elapsed/args.num_samples*1000:.1f}ms per sample")
    print()

    # Benchmark 2: select() method (fast)
    elapsed = benchmark_hf_dataset_select(dataset_simple, args.num_samples, args.horizon)
    print(f"2. hf_dataset.select(indices)[key] (OpenPi's fast approach):")
    print(f"   {elapsed:.3f}s total, {elapsed/args.num_samples*1000:.1f}ms per sample")
    print()

    # Benchmark 3: Direct indexing (slow - LeRobot v3.0's approach)
    elapsed = benchmark_hf_dataset_direct_indexing(dataset_simple, args.num_samples, args.horizon)
    print(f"3. hf_dataset[indices][key] (LeRobot v3.0's slow approach):")
    print(f"   {elapsed:.3f}s total, {elapsed/args.num_samples*1000:.1f}ms per sample")
    print()

    # Benchmark 4: Full LeRobotDataset with delta_timestamps
    elapsed = benchmark_lerobot_dataset(dataset_with_delta, args.num_samples)
    print(f"4. LeRobotDataset[i] with delta_timestamps (what training uses):")
    print(f"   {elapsed:.3f}s total, {elapsed/args.num_samples*1000:.1f}ms per sample")
    print()

    print("=" * 60)
    print("ANALYSIS")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Calculate speedup
    t_select = benchmark_hf_dataset_select(dataset_simple, 10, args.horizon) / 10
    t_direct = benchmark_hf_dataset_direct_indexing(dataset_simple, 10, args.horizon) / 10
    speedup = t_direct / t_select if t_select > 0 else 0

    print(f"select() is {speedup:.1f}x faster than direct indexing")
    print()

    # Estimate full training impact
    total_frames = meta.total_frames
    t_per_sample = elapsed / args.num_samples
    estimated_epoch_time = total_frames * t_per_sample
    print(f"Estimated time per epoch with current LeRobotDataset:")
    print(f"  {estimated_epoch_time/3600:.1f} hours ({estimated_epoch_time/60:.0f} minutes)")
    print()

    # Estimate with fix
    t_fast = benchmark_hf_dataset_select(dataset_simple, args.num_samples, args.horizon) / args.num_samples
    estimated_fast_epoch = total_frames * t_fast
    print(f"Estimated time per epoch with select() fix:")
    print(f"  {estimated_fast_epoch/3600:.2f} hours ({estimated_fast_epoch/60:.0f} minutes)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Environment

- LeRobot version: v3.0 (latest main)
- Dataset format: parquet (images stored in parquet, not video)
- Python: 3.10
- Platform: Linux

items.body:
**Hey** 👋, we faced a critical bug using lerobot dataset.

**LeRobotDataset is not revision-safe on shared storage: concurrent loads of different HF revisions overwrite each other**

**Minimal reproducible example:** [https://gist.github.com/AdilZouitine/7c1b50c0ef7be3c34ce25ec92ea7cb03](https://gist.github.com/AdilZouitine/7c1b50c0ef7be3c34ce25ec92ea7cb03)

**TLDR**: Concurrent reading of the same Lerobot dataset with different Hugging Face revisions on a shared cluster can cause a running process (using one revision) to suddenly switch to the structure of the other revision being loaded, leading to crashes and non-reproducible results.

**Context:**

Training models in a shared computing environment often involves multiple users accessing the same datasets simultaneously. This scenario is particularly problematic when leveraging Hugging Face dataset versioning.

**The Problematic Scenario:**

Consider this common situation:

* **Engineer Alice** is training a model using dataset "foo" at the main revision (the latest version, perhaps with a new column).  
* **Engineer Bob** is training with the *same* dataset but at an older, specific revision, e.g., `b59010db93eb6cc3cf06ef2f7cae1bbe62b726d9` (a version *without* the new column).

**Expected vs. Actual Behavior:**

The **expected behavior** is that Alice's training uses the main instance and Bob's uses the instance corresponding to revision `b59010db93eb6cc3cf06ef2f7cae1bbe62b726d9`, maintaining isolation.

However, **in practice, this isolation fails.**

1. Alice starts her training using the main revision, and it proceeds correctly.  
2. Twenty minutes later, Bob starts his training using the older revision, `b59010db93eb6cc3cf06ef2f7cae1bbe62b726d9`.  
3. As soon as Bob loads his older revision, the shared dataset changes its structure on the fly.

Alice's ongoing training **instantly crashes** because the columns she was relying on from the main revision are suddenly missing.

**Consequences:**

This unexpected dynamic change of the dataset due to concurrent reading of different versions creates severe issues:

* **Lack of Reproducibility:** Experiences cannot be reliably reproduced.  
* **Critical Determinism Problem:** Your underlying data literally changes during runtime, undermining the integrity of the training process.

**Root Cause Analysis**

The issue originates from a design mismatch between how `huggingface_hub`'s `snapshot_download` handles revisions via its two storage modes, and how `lerobot`'s `LeRobotDataset` chooses between them.

The two storage modes of `snapshot_download`

`huggingface_hub`'s `snapshot_download` function has two fundamentally different storage strategies, controlled by the `local_dir` parameter:

**1\. Cache mode (`local_dir=None` ; the default):**

When `local_dir` is not provided, `snapshot_download` uses the HF Hub cache system at `~/.cache/huggingface/hub/`. This system is **revision-safe by design**. It stores files in a content-addressed blob store (`blobs/`) and creates per-commit-hash snapshot directories (`snapshots/<commit_hash>/`) containing symlinks into the blob store. Each revision resolves to a different commit hash, and thus to a different snapshot directory. Two processes reading different revisions read from completely isolated directory trees.

The returned path looks like:

```
~/.cache/huggingface/hub/datasets--<org>--<repo>/snapshots/9865698e28ce6d511487f4b0ed0607b22246edd6
```

**2\. Local-dir mode (`local_dir=<some path>`):**

When `local_dir` is provided, `snapshot_download` bypasses the cache system entirely. Instead, it replicates the repository's file tree directly into the provided directory. The function downloads each file to `local_dir/<relative_path>` (via `_hf_hub_download_to_local_dir`) and stores lightweight metadata (commit hash \+ etag) in a hidden `.cache/huggingface/download/` folder inside `local_dir`.   
Critically, **the revision is not encoded in the directory path**. The function returns `str(os.path.realpath(local_dir))` regardless of which revision was requested.

This means: if two calls to `snapshot_download` target the same `local_dir` but different revisions, the second call **overwrites the first's files in-place**. The metadata files are updated to reflect the new commit hash, but the actual data files at `local_dir/data/chunk-000/episode_000000.parquet` are silently replaced. Any process that had an open handle or a cached path to these files will now read the wrong revision's data.

**How LeRobot triggers the unsafe mode**

`LeRobotDataset` (and `LeRobotDatasetMetadata`) **always** uses `local_dir` mode. In `pull_from_repo`:

```py
# lerobot/datasets/dataset_metadata.py:145-152
snapshot_download(
    self.repo_id,
    repo_type="dataset",
    revision=self.revision,
    local_dir=self.root,  # <-- always provided
    ...
)
```

Where `self.root` defaults to:

```py
self.root = Path(root) if root is not None else HF_LEROBOT_HOME / repo_id
# e.g. ~/.cache/huggingface/lerobot/AdilZtn/pick_and_place_intermediate_30_ep
```

Notice: the root path contains the `repo_id` but **not the revision**. Every revision of the same dataset resolves to the same local directory. This is the core of the problem.

The race condition, step by step

1. **Alice** starts training with `revision="main"` (commit `9865698e`). `snapshot_download` writes the main revision's files (which include a `test` column in the parquet data) to `~/.cache/huggingface/lerobot/<repo_id>/.` The metadata files in `.cache/huggingface/download/` record `commit_hash=9865698e`.  
2. Alice's training loop periodically reads from `~/.cache/huggingface/lerobot/<repo_id>/data/chunk-000/episode_000000.parquet`. Everything works.  
3. **Bob** starts training with `revision="b59010db"` (an older commit without the `test` column). `snapshot_download` is called with the **same** `local_dir`. The function checks the metadata: the stored `commit_hash` is `9865698e`, which doesn't match `b59010db`. So it re-downloads.  
4. For each file, `_hf_hub_download_to_local_dir` calls `paths.file_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)` to delete the existing file, then downloads the older revision's version in its place. This happens under a `WeakFileLock`, but the lock only protects the download itself; it does not coordinate with readers in other processes.

Alice's next read of the parquet file returns the **old revision's schema**; the `test` column is gone. Her training crashes or, worse, silently produces garbage.

**Why the "no `local_dir`" experiment doesn't have the issue**

We tested downloading the dataset directly when `huggingface_hub` is called without `local_dir` specified:

```py
root = Path(snapshot_download(REPO_ID, repo_type="dataset", revision=revision))
```

This uses the cache mode. Bob's path resolves to `.../snapshots/9865698e.../`, Alice's resolves to `.../snapshots/b59010db.../`. The two snapshot directories are independent. The blob store may share deduplicated content, but the snapshot paths never alias, and no file in Bob's tree is ever overwritten by Alice's download.

The second experiment, `local_dir`, is explicitly provided:

```py
root = Path(snapshot_download(REPO_ID, repo_type="dataset", revision=revision, local_dir=local_dir))
```

This forces local-dir mode. Both revisions write to the same flat directory (`/Users/adil@uma.bot/.cache/tmp_huggingface`). The second download overwrites the first's parquet file, reproducing the exact same corruption observed through `LeRobotDataset`.

The bug is not in `huggingface_hub` per se; `local_dir` mode is documented as being "optimized for regularly pulling the latest version of a repository," not for concurrent multi-revision access. The issue is that `LeRobotDataset` unconditionally uses this mode without encoding the revision in the directory path, making concurrent multi-revision training on shared clusters unsafe.

**We must avoid adding the revision to the root path as a fix. Doing so would lead to dataset duplication, multiplying hard drive memory by the number of revisions, and eliminating the benefits of the Hugging Face tech.**

items.title: fix(train): normalize relative actions with relative action statistics

labels.name: tests
labels.description: Problems with test coverage, failures, or improvements to testing

items.body:
## Summary / Motivation

Training with `use_relative_actions=True` on a dataset whose stats were never recomputed for relative actions silently succeeds. `RelativeActionsProcessorStep` runs before the normalizer, so the model trains on `action - observation.state` while [`lerobot_train.py:509`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_train.py#L509) normalizes it with the **absolute** action stats. No warning, no check. It is the wrong distribution rather than a poor summary of one, so every normalization mode is affected — `MEAN_STD` (pi0, pi0_fast), `MIN_MAX` (vla_jepa), `QUANTILES` (pi0.5).

The only defence today is remembering to run `lerobot-edit-dataset --operation.type recompute_stats --operation.relative_action true` beforehand. This PR does it automatically for any dataset the training script can scan.

## Related issues

- Related: #3832 (ARCH-05)

## What changed

- `lerobot-train` recomputes the action stats over the dataset's relative chunks via the existing `compute_relative_action_stats`. `observation.state` stats are untouched.
- Streaming datasets warn and keep today's behaviour. The guard is load-bearing: `StreamingLeRobotDataset` does expose `.hf_dataset`, but `np.array(iterable_ds["action"])` returns a 0-d `object` array instead of raising.

No breaking changes; the offline `lerobot-edit-dataset` route still works.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

3 tests in `tests/scripts/test_lerobot_train_batch_preprocessing.py`: flag off → stats untouched; flag on → action stats describe the relative distribution and excluded dims keep their absolute spread; streaming → warns and falls back.

```bash
pytest -sv tests/scripts/ tests/policies/test_relative_actions.py     # 62 passed
pre-commit run --files src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_train.py tests/scripts/test_lerobot_train_batch_preprocessing.py
```

Pushing a real batch through the pi0 preprocessor on `lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace` (`chunk_size=50`, `relative_exclude_joints=["gripper"]`, 474k relative action samples), the share of actions landing outside `[-1, 1]` goes from 70.5% to 28.4% under `MEAN_STD`, 49.8% → 0.0% under `MIN_MAX` and 49.9% → 2.0% under `QUANTILES`; the worst dimension was offset by −5.34σ.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run`)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [ ] Documentation updated — `action_representations.mdx` still presents the offline `recompute_stats` as a prerequisite; happy to fold that in or follow up
- [x] CI is green
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: #

## Reviewer notes

- **Why not just fail loudly instead?** That was the first option I looked at, but nothing in a dataset says whether its stats are relative. `lerobot-edit-dataset --operation.relative_action true` rewrites `meta/stats.json` and nothing else — I diffed the result and `info.json` is byte-identical; the `chunk_size` and `exclude_joints` it used are not recorded anywhere. The values are not a tell either: on `lerobot/libero`, whose actions are already deltas, absolute `mean[0]` is 0.063 against 0.086 for relative. openpi can raise here because its norm stats are a per-config artifact (`assets/<config>/<repo_id>/norm_stats.json`), whereas LeRobot has one `stats.json` shared by every config. If recording that provenance in the dataset and failing on a mismatch is the design you prefer, I am glad to implement that instead.
- Stats are computed on every rank rather than on rank 0 and broadcast. `compute_relative_action_stats` is deterministic so the result is the same; broadcasting would only save each rank loading the action/state columns. Happy to add it.
- That function loads the full columns into memory (2.1 s on `lerobot/libero`), which will matter at DROID scale — a frame cap would be a reasonable follow-up.
- `chunk_size` comes from `policy.chunk_size`, removing the mismatch the offline route allowed. All five configs exposing `use_relative_actions` define it.
- `aggregate_feature_stats` is untouched; dataset-level quantile aggregation is #4156's territory.

---

*Disclosure per [AI_POLICY.md](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md): I used an AI assistant to explore the call paths and draft this description. The diagnosis, fix, tests and every number above I produced and verified by running the code myself.*

## Summary / Motivation

Dataset statistics compute variance as `E[x**2] - E[x]**2`. Cancellation can erase real variation: float32 values `[10000, 10001, 10002]` produce a standard deviation of zero instead of approximately `0.8165`. Float64 inputs with a larger offset have the same problem, affecting the statistics used for normalization.

Accumulate centered second moments in float64 and combine batches with the parallel variance formula. Keep means relative to a fixed per-feature origin so large float64 offsets do not round away small variations. The accumulator retains only per-feature running state.

## Related issues

Searched open issues and PRs for variance and RunningQuantileStats fixes. The open histogram-merge PR #3801 addresses global quantiles, a separate problem.

## What changed

- Preserve small variations around large means in single and multiple batches.
- Cover float32 and float64 inputs, uneven batches, individual samples, constant features, input preservation, and the public feature-statistics helper.
- Verify that 54,550 identical float32 and float64 vectors retain the exact mean and normalize to zero, in one batch and five batches.
- Cover small float64 variations around a non-integer offset of `1e12` across single, uneven, and one-sample batches.
- Reject empty and mismatched batches without changing accumulated statistics.

## How was this tested

- The original seven regression cases failed before the fix. Both constant-float32 cases also fail on main and pass with this branch. Seven additional float64 regressions failed on the previous PR head and pass after shifting the means.
- `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/datasets/test_compute_stats.py tests/datasets/test_quantiles_dataset_integration.py tests/processor/test_normalize_processor.py -q`: **130 passed, 1 skipped** on Windows, Python 3.12, CPU.
- CI-pinned Ruff formatting and linting, plus all applicable pre-commit hooks, passed on the changed files.
- An interleaved benchmark on 100,000 × 8 arrays measured about 68 ms for float32 and 73 ms for float64, versus 67 ms and 72 ms on the previous PR head. This is a local smoke benchmark.
- Before opening this PR, all four workflows passed on commit `c53bb21ba78cea302d1026de9ff0ff243a50f167`: [Quality](https://github.com/dipeshbabu/lerobot/actions/runs/35647373032), [Fast Tests](https://github.com/dipeshbabu/lerobot/actions/runs/35647378780), [Security](https://github.com/dipeshbabu/lerobot/actions/runs/35647383684), and [Full Tests](https://github.com/dipeshbabu/lerobot/actions/runs/35647388516). items.body:
## Title

fix(processor): support explicit relative state→action index map

## Summary / Motivation

Relative-action conversion computed the base as `state[..., :action_dim]`, which
silently assumes the first `action_dim` channels of `observation.state` are
positionally aligned with the action. That only holds when the state is a
prefix-aligned copy of the action and breaks for non-prefix layouts (interleaved
`[pos, vel]` per joint; state augmented with force/torque, EE pose, contact
flags). When it breaks, the wrong state columns are subtracted at preprocess and
added back at postprocess, so the model trains on corrupted relative targets and
eval produces wrong absolute actions — with no error or warning.

This adds an optional, explicit `state_action_index_map` (entry `i` is the
`observation.state` column that action dim `i` is relative to), used symmetrically
by `RelativeActionsProcessorStep` (preprocess) and `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep`
(postprocess), and threaded through the relative-action stats path and the
pi0 / pi0.5 / pi0-fast configs, so train-time targets, stats, and runtime
transforms all use the same base. A validation guard raises on length/range
mismatch so misalignment fails loudly.

**Trade-off / design note:** name-based auto-resolution (matching
`action_feature_names` ↔ `observation.state` names) was intentionally deferred to
keep this diff focused and avoid an implicit default-behavior change. Happy to add
it as a follow-up.

## Related issues

- Fixes / Closes: #3863
- Related: #3960 (alternative approach to the same issue)

## What changed

- `processor/relative_action_processor.py`: new `_state_base_offset` helper;
  optional `state_index_map` arg on `to_relative_actions` / `to_absolute_actions`;
  `state_action_index_map` field + `_resolve_state_index_map` validation guard on
  `RelativeActionsProcessorStep`; `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep` reuses the same map.
- `datasets/compute_stats.py` + `datasets/dataset_tools.py`: thread the map through
  relative-action stats (`compute_relative_action_stats`, `recompute_stats`).
- `policies/pi0|pi05|pi0_fast` configs + processors: expose/forward
  `relative_state_index_map`.
- `scripts/lerobot_train.py` + `scripts/lerobot_edit_dataset.py`: forward the map so
  train targets and recomputed stats use the same base.
- Tests + pi0 / pi0.5 README config tables.
- **Breaking changes:** none. With no map (`None`), behavior is byte-identical to the
  previous `state[:action_dim]` prefix path — no migration needed.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)
