items.title: fix(processor): compose xyz+rot6d poses in SE(3) for relative actions
items.body:
> **Depends on [#4779](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/4779) — review that one first.** This branch is stacked on it and its commits show up here. I will rebase onto `main` once #4779 lands.

## Summary / Motivation

[#4779](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/4779) makes `to_relative_actions` compose `[x, y, z, rx, ry, rz]` poses in SE(3) instead of subtracting them. That covers axis-angle, but GR00T also declares `xyz+rot6d` as a rotation type ([`policies/groot/utils.py:99`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/policies/groot/utils.py#L99)) — nine dimensions, xyz plus the first two rotation-matrix rows.

GR00T's own EEF path composes those correctly. The generic fallback does not: when a checkpoint carries non-relative statistics, [`processor_groot.py:1237`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/policies/groot/processor_groot.py#L1237) drops to the shared `RelativeActionsProcessorStep`, which subtracts all nine dimensions.

**This fails more quietly than the axis-angle case.** `rot6d_to_matrix` runs Gram-Schmidt, so any six numbers come back as an orthonormal matrix with `det = 1`. No `NaN`, no exception — just a plausible, wrong rotation.

## Related issues

- Related: #4779, #3983, #3832 (ARCH-05)

## What changed

- A pose group's **length now selects the rotation encoding**: six for `[x, y, z, rx, ry, rz]` (unchanged), nine for `[x, y, z, r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23]`. No new config field.
- Nine-index groups are composed **as matrices throughout**: a 6-D rotation is the first two rows of a rotation matrix, so `inv(R_ref) @ R_target` is a transpose and two matmuls. No quaternion detour, and no `matrix_to_quaternion` with its branch selection near `pi`. The action does not widen.
- `rotation_6d_to_matrix` / `matrix_to_rotation_6d` live in `lerobot/utils/rotation.py`, next to the NumPy `Rotation` class that module already provides. They are torch because the step runs on batched GPU tensors and has to keep their device and dtype.
- **The reference pose is checked for orthonormality** (tolerance `1e-3`). It comes from the dataset or the robot, so its rows are orthonormal by construction; if they are not, the group is not addressing an `xyz+rot6d` pose in the state and the composition would silently return a wrong rotation. Predicted poses are not checked — orthonormalizing those is the point.

Empty by default, so existing behaviour is unchanged.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

```bash
pytest -sv tests/policies/test_relative_actions.py tests/processor/ tests/datasets/test_compute_stats.py
# 554 passed, 55 skipped
```

**Is the new path correct?** On 512 random pose pairs encoded as `xyz+rot6d`, the relative rotation matches `inv(R_state) @ R_action` to `7.5e-14°` and the round-trip to `3.3e-15`.

**How wrong is subtracting rot6d?** Over 5,000 random orientation pairs, decoding `a6 - s6` through `rot6d_to_matrix`:

| | median | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| error vs `inv(R_state) @ R_action` | **134.8°** | 171.1° | 180° |

Zero `NaN`; every result is a valid rotation matrix with `det = 1`.

Unlike axis-angle, **the error does not shrink with the relative rotation**:

| relative rotation | subtracting rot6d | subtracting a rotation vector |
|---|---|---|
| 5° | **131.7°** | 4.7° |
| 20° | **132.9°** | 18.2° |
| 60° | **131.0°** | 49.5° |

Once the reference orientation is away from identity, even a small motion is wrong by a third of a turn.

3 tests added: round-trip and correctness for a nine-index group, the reference-orthonormality guard, and group-width validation.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run`)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [ ] Documentation updated — `action_representations.mdx` gained an SE(3) section in #4779; I will extend it with the nine-index layout once that one settles
- [ ] CI is green
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: #

## Reviewer notes

- **Scope.** This deliberately does not touch GR00T's native path, which is already correct, nor the general state→action index mapping that [#4111](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/4111) is working on. The orthonormality check only catches a misaligned group; it does not fix the alignment.
- **rot6d lands on the worst case of the float32 statistics accumulation.** Statistics need no change here — #4779 made `compute_relative_action_stats` delegate to `to_relative_actions`, so nine-index groups work as they are, and on a synthetic end-effector set the normalized actions come out at `std 1.006`, `|mean| 0.0002`. But two of the ten dimensions are off by 2.4-3.5%, and they are `r11` and `r22`: the diagonal of a *relative* rotation matrix, which is near identity, so those entries sit at `0.98` with `std 0.027` — a mean-to-std ratio of 35.

  `RunningQuantileStats` accumulates in float32 ([`compute_stats.py:68`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/datasets/compute_stats.py#L68)) and takes `variance = E[x^2] - E[x]^2` ([`:127`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/datasets/compute_stats.py#L127)). At that ratio a `2.7e-5` error in the accumulated mean becomes a 3% error in the std; accumulating in float64 instead drops both dimensions to `0.00%`. Axis-angle and translation have ratios near `0.1` and are unaffected, so this only becomes visible once rot6d is in play.

  Pre-existing and out of scope here, but worth knowing that this representation walks straight into it. Happy to send the float64 accumulation as its own PR.

- **Why not a rotation library.** `lerobot` depends on none of kornia, roma or pytorch3d, and `scipy` is an optional extra (`scipy-dep`) that is NumPy-only, so it cannot run inside a processor step on GPU tensors. `lerobot/utils/rotation.py` already exists for exactly this reason — "replace scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation" — and that is where the two new helpers went. Happy to swap them for a dependency if you would rather add one.
- #4132 does this through `rotvec_to_rotation_6d` / `rotation_6d_to_rotvec`, which route a 6-D rotation through a quaternion. Composing the matrices directly gives the same answer to `3.6e-15` and drops the two most delicate functions, so I did not carry those over.
- Statistics follow automatically: #4779 made `compute_relative_action_stats` delegate to `to_relative_actions`, so the offline path picks up nine-index groups with no change.

---

The converters are lifted from #4132 as noted; the wiring, the guard, the tests and every measurement above I produced and verified by running the code myself.*

## Summary / Motivation

`to_relative_actions` subtracts every masked dimension:

```python
actions[..., :dims] -= state_offset
```

That is right for scalar quantities — joint angles, positions, grippers — but rotations compose by multiplication, not subtraction. The relative rotation is `inv(R_state) @ R_action`; subtracting two axis-angle vectors is not that, and the gap grows with the relative rotation and with the action horizon (measurements in the reviewer notes).

The same repository already does it correctly in two places, so this PR just brings the generic step in line:

- GR00T's EEF path composes `reference @ relative` ([`policies/groot/utils.py:209-218`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/policies/groot/utils.py#L209-L218)) — but only on its native path; whenever it falls back to the shared `RelativeActionsProcessorStep` ([`processor_groot.py:1237`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/policies/groot/processor_groot.py#L1237)) the rotations are subtracted again
- UMI, where this chunk-relative trajectory representation comes from, composes homogeneous matrices — [`convert_pose_mat_rep`](https://github.com/real-stanford/universal_manipulation_interface/blob/d095ba9590df789df5189eea5ee7e431689038a6/diffusion_policy/common/pose_repr_util.py#L48-L78) returns `inv(base_pose_mat) @ pose_mat` for `pose_rep='relative'`. It keeps an older variant under `pose_rep='rel'` that subtracts the translation, and its own comment calls that one `# legacy buggy implementation / # for compatibility` — and even that variant still composes the rotation with a matrix product rather than subtracting it

## Related issues

- Related: #3983, #3832 (ARCH-05)

## What changed

- `to_relative_actions` / `to_absolute_actions` take `se3_pose_groups`: action index groups shaped `[x, y, z, rx, ry, rz]` (axis-angle) that are composed as `inv(T_state) @ T_action` / `T_state @ T_relative` instead of subtracted. Quaternion-based, batched, pure torch; the quaternion helpers live in `lerobot/utils/rotation.py` next to the NumPy `Rotation` class (torch, `[w, x, y, z]` — the processor runs on batched GPU tensors, and none of kornia/roma/pytorch3d is a dependency while `scipy` is an optional, NumPy-only extra).
- `RelativeActionsProcessorStep` carries the groups; `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep` reads them back off its paired step.
- `compute_relative_action_stats` delegates to `to_relative_actions`, so the offline statistics and the training pipeline cannot describe different distributions. Exposed as `lerobot-edit-dataset --operation.relative_se3_pose_groups`.
- `relative_se3_pose_groups` added to every policy that builds the shared step — pi0, pi0.5, pi0_fast, GR00T, VLA-JEPA and FLUX3 — and wired into their processors. GR00T is the one with public evidence of being affected: it declares `xyz+rotvec` as a rotation type ([`groot/utils.py:101`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/policies/groot/utils.py#L101)) and composes poses correctly in `relative_eef_to_absolute`, but whenever it falls back to the shared step ([`processor_groot.py:1237`](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/main/src/lerobot/policies/groot/processor_groot.py#L1237)) the rotations were subtracted again. Its relative-stats helper takes the groups too, so the two paths agree.

**Empty by default**, so every existing policy and checkpoint is bit-identical. Groups are validated: six indices, in range, non-overlapping, and inside the relative mask.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

```bash
pytest -sv tests/policies/test_relative_actions.py tests/processor/ tests/datasets/test_compute_stats.py
# 592 passed, 14 skipped
```

**How wrong is the current subtraction, and when does it matter?**

Over uniformly random orientation pairs the subtracted vector is off by a **median of 80.8°** (p90 137°). The error scales with the relative rotation — 25.8° for a 60° relative rotation, 2.3° for 5° — so a task whose tool orientation barely moves barely notices.

`lerobot/libero` is at the other end. Its state axis-angle has `‖r‖` between 2.97 and 4.04 rad: the gripper points down, which is a half-turn, so the trajectories sit on the axis-angle double cover at `pi`. Comparing the two relative targets over every valid `chunk_size=50` window (98 episodes, 27k frames):

| | median | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| true in-chunk rotation (the signal) | 8.0° | 37.5° | — |
| subtraction vs SE(3) (the error) | **13.1°** | **72°** | **180°** |

2.8% of chunks differ by more than 90°. The error is larger than the signal it is supposed to carry.

**A success-rate A/B is running** — PI0.5 finetuned on LIBERO twice from `lerobot/pi05_libero_base`, identical except `relative_se3_pose_groups`, following the recipe in `docs/source/pi05.mdx`. I will post the numbers when it finishes.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run`)
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [x] Documentation updated — `action_representations.mdx` claimed relative actions work in EE space while its example carried no orientation at all; it now shows how to declare pose groups and recompute the matching statistics
- [x] CI is green
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: #

## Reviewer notes

- **Scope, and what follows.** The quaternion helpers and `to_relative_se3_pose` / `to_absolute_se3_pose` are lifted from [#4132](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/4132), which landed on a `codex/` branch and never reached `main`. This PR takes only the axis-angle layout, `[x, y, z, rx, ry, rz]`. Two things are deliberately left for later:

  - **`xyz+rot6d` inputs** — GR00T declares that layout too, and subtracting those nine dimensions is worse than subtracting a rotation vector, because Gram-Schmidt turns any six numbers into a valid rotation and the error never shrinks with the motion. [#4780](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/4780) is stacked on this branch and does it.
  - **`se3_6d` outputs** — #4132's other mode, which re-encodes the *result* as a continuous 6-D vector. It removes the `pi` discontinuity from the regression target, which is where it hurts: a rotation vector gives two valid answers for the same rotation, so the network is asked to fit both. I would like to port it once these two settle.

    One thing to flag now, since this PR fixes the interface: a pose group indexes the action and the state with the same indices, which holds while both are six wide (here) or both nine (#4780). `se3_6d` breaks that — the action widens to nine while the state stays six — so #4132 slices the action with a running cursor instead. Widening the state to match would be cleaner, but that is an observation change: for PI0.5 the state is discretized into 256 bins and written into the prompt, so its width is part of the checkpoint contract.

- **The pose layout has to be stated twice, and nothing checks the two agree.** `lerobot-edit-dataset --operation.relative_se3_pose_groups=...` computes the statistics for a layout, then `--policy.relative_se3_pose_groups=...` states the same layout again at train time. `recompute_stats` records none of it, so a mismatch — different groups, a different `chunk_size`, or relative statistics used with `use_relative_actions=false` — is silent. That is the shape of the problem #3832 (ARCH-05) describes, and the fix is to let the dataset declare the layout in `meta/info.json` and have `make_policy` read it back, the way `action_feature_names` is already populated from dataset metadata. **I have that working and will send it as a follow-up** rather than grow this PR.
- **Three fields, six configs.** `use_relative_actions` and `relative_exclude_joints` were already declared separately in every policy config; this PR adds `relative_se3_pose_groups` beside them. Hoisting all three into a shared mixin is a config refactor rather than a correctness fix, so it is also a follow-up — say if you would rather have it here.
- **Canonical rotation vectors.** SE(3) composition returns the representative with `‖r‖ <= pi`, so a dataset storing unwrapped rotation vectors gets back the same rotation but not the same vector.
- Declaring pose layout by index group follows GR00T's `action_configs` (`{"rep": "relative", "type": "eef", "rotation_type": "xyz+rotvec"}`), which it reads from checkpoint-side modality config rather than the LeRobot config.

---

The quaternion helpers are lifted from #4132 as noted; the wiring, the validation, the tests and every measurement above I produced and verified by running the code myself.*

## Summary / Motivation

Dataset-level quantile statistics (`q01, q10, q50, q90, q99`) are currently produced by **count-weighted averaging of per-episode quantiles** in `aggregate_feature_stats`. This is statistically incorrect: the mean of per-episode `q01` values is not the global `q01`. Averaging pulls the distribution tails inward (`q01` too high, `q99` too low).

This matters for quantile-normalized policies (pi0 / pi0.5), which map `[q01, q99] -> [-1, 1]` **without clipping**. With inward-biased quantiles, a large fraction of real actions/states normalize to values well outside `[-1, 1]`.

Exact global quantiles cannot be reconstructed from already-summarized stats dicts (they need the underlying data/histograms), so this PR adds a streaming **histogram-merge** path that yields true global quantiles in a single pass with bounded memory — the same "single global running histogram" approach used by openpi and by the repo's existing `compute_relative_action_stats`.

## Related issues

- Related: N/A

## What changed

- **`RunningQuantileStats.merge(other)`** (new): re-bins both accumulators' histograms onto their union range and sums the counts; `mean`/`std`/`min`/`max`/`count` combine exactly. The resulting quantiles are global, accurate to histogram resolution — not a count-weighted average.
- **New helpers**: `aggregate_quantile_stats(list)`, `compute_feature_running_stats(...)`, `feature_stats_from_running(...)`. `get_feature_stats` is refactored to reuse them (no behavior change). All exported from `lerobot.datasets`.
- **`scripts/augment_dataset_quantile_stats.py`**: now streams each episode into per-feature running histograms and merges them instead of calling `aggregate_stats`, producing true global quantiles with bounded memory (one merged accumulator per feature). Run with `--overwrite` to upgrade datasets that already carry biased quantiles.
- **`aggregate_feature_stats`**: its quantile aggregation remains a documented approximation for summary-only callers (recording / multi-dataset combine), since exact global quantiles can't be recovered there. It now carries an explanatory comment and emits a one-time warning pointing to the recompute path. `mean`/`std`/`min`/`max` aggregation is unchanged.

No breaking changes. Existing stats files remain valid; the augment script (with `--overwrite`) upgrades biased quantiles to correct global ones.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

- New unit tests in `tests/datasets/test_compute_stats.py`:
  - `test_merge_matches_single_pass` — merged per-chunk accumulators equal a single pass; mean/std/min/max exact, quantiles match `np.quantile`.
  - `test_merge_yields_global_quantiles_unlike_averaging` — on a bimodal two-episode distribution, merge recovers the true global `q01/q99` (matches `np.quantile`) while averaging per-episode quantiles is >10x worse.
  - empty/identity merges, compatibility validation, and the new-helper round-trips.
- Commands:
  - `pre-commit run --files src/lerobot/datasets/compute_stats.py src/lerobot/datasets/__init__.py src/lerobot/scripts/augment_dataset_quantile_stats.py tests/datasets/test_compute_stats.py` → all hooks pass (ruff, typos, bandit, mypy, …).
  - `pytest -q tests/datasets/test_compute_stats.py tests/datasets/test_quantiles_dataset_integration.py tests/processor/test_normalize_processor.py` → **118 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Manual end-to-end check on a synthetic 4-episode dataset (per-episode means -9/-3/+3/+9): the augment script's merged `q01` matches `np.quantile` to <0.05, whereas the per-episode-averaged `q01` was off by ~8.6.

## Checklist (required before merge)

- [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run -a`) — run on the changed files; all hooks pass
- [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest`) — stats / quantile-integration / normalize suites (118 passed, 1 skipped); commands above
- [ ] Documentation updated — n/a for user-facing docs; inline docstrings + augment-script module docstring updated
- [ ] CI is green — pending CI on this PR
- [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: # (TODO: add link)

## Reviewer notes

- Focus areas: `RunningQuantileStats.merge` (histogram re-binning math) and the rewritten `compute_quantile_stats_for_dataset` in the augment script.
- Design note: `aggregate_feature_stats` still averages quantiles for summary-only callers because exact global quantiles can't be reconstructed from per-episode summaries. The new one-time `logging.warning` flags this; happy to soften it to a docstring-only note if preferred.
- This PR intentionally does **not** change the live recording path (`save_episode` → `aggregate_stats`); freshly recorded datasets still get approximate quantiles at record time and should be upgraded with the augment script before training quantile-normalized policies. A follow-up could thread running-histogram accumulators through recording for end-to-end correctness if desired.

# PR: feat(policies): add relative action support for pi0, pi0.5, and pi0_fast

## Type / Scope

- **Type**: Feature
- **Scope**: policies/pi0, policies/pi05, policies/pi0_fast, processor, datasets

## Summary / Motivation

OpenPI trains pi0/pi0.5 models using what UMI ([Chi et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10329)) calls **relative trajectory** actions — every action in the chunk is an offset from the robot's current state at prediction time, not from the previous action. This avoids error accumulation (unlike true deltas) and doesn't require a global coordinate frame (unlike absolute actions):

| Representation | Definition | Error behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Absolute | `action[t]` in global coordinates | Requires precise calibration |
| Delta | `action[t]` relative to `action[t-1]` | Accumulates error over time |
| **Relative trajectory** | `action[t]` relative to current state at `t=0` | No error accumulation, no calibration needed |

OpenPI's `DeltaActions` class is somewhat misleadingly named — what it implements is UMI's relative trajectory representation. We use the term **relative actions** throughout LeRobot to match the correct semantics.

LeRobot's pi0 family was missing this transform, causing a distribution mismatch when fine-tuning from OpenPI pretrained weights and sometimes resulting in jittery motion during inference. This PR adds an optional `use_relative_actions: bool` config flag to all three pi policies.

## Related issues

- Related: https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/2891#issuecomment-3857478982

## What changed

### Processor pipeline

- **`relative_action_processor.py`** (new): Added `to_relative_actions()` / `to_absolute_actions()` functions, `RelativeActionsProcessorStep` (preprocessor) and `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep` (postprocessor). Supports `relative_exclude_joints` to keep specific dimensions (e.g. gripper) in absolute space.
- **`processor/__init__.py`**: Updated exports for new processor steps.

### Policy configs & processors

- **`configuration_pi0.py` / `configuration_pi05.py` / `configuration_pi0_fast.py`**: Added `use_relative_actions`, `relative_exclude_joints`, and `action_feature_names` config fields.
- **`processor_pi0.py` / `processor_pi05.py` / `processor_pi0_fast.py`**: Added `RelativeActionsProcessorStep` to all three preprocessor pipelines and `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep` to postprocessors.
- **`factory.py`**: Added `_reconnect_relative_absolute_steps()` to wire the postprocessor's `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep` back to the preprocessor's cached state after deserialization. Stores `action_feature_names` from dataset metadata on the config.

### Dataset stats

- **`compute_stats.py`**: Added `compute_relative_action_stats()` — samples random action chunks, converts to relative space (offset from current state for each chunk), and computes statistics. This matches what the model sees during training.
- **`dataset_tools.py`**: Extended `recompute_stats()` with `relative_action`, `relative_exclude_joints`, and `chunk_size` parameters. When `relative_action=True`, delegates action stats to `compute_relative_action_stats`.

### CLI

- **`lerobot_edit_dataset.py`**: Added `recompute_stats` operation so users can precompute relative action stats from the command line:
  ```bash
  lerobot-edit-dataset \
      --repo_id your_dataset \
      --operation.type recompute_stats \
      --operation.relative_action true \
      --operation.chunk_size 50 \
      --operation.relative_exclude_joints "['gripper']"
  ```

## Reviewer notes

- **Terminology**: We use "relative actions" (not "delta") following UMI's taxonomy ([Chi et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10329)). Each action in the chunk is an offset from the current state, not from the previous action — this avoids error accumulation. OpenPI's upstream class is named `DeltaActions` but implements relative trajectory semantics.
- The relative conversion lives in the **processor pipeline** (`RelativeActionsProcessorStep` / `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep`). The `AbsoluteActionsProcessorStep` reads cached state from its paired `RelativeActionsProcessorStep` — the wiring is done in `factory.py::_reconnect_relative_absolute_steps()` after deserialization.
- `relative_exclude_joints` allows keeping specific joints (e.g. gripper) in absolute space. The mask is built from `action_feature_names` on the config.
- Relative action stats must be precomputed before training (via `lerobot-edit-dataset --operation.type recompute_stats --operation.relative_action true`). The training script no longer computes them on the fly to avoid NCCL timeouts in multi-GPU setups.
